newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds aim to take out 115-23 high.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds aim to take out 115-23 high.

text.p: September T-bonds will suffer a slight setback towards 114-18 near term before heading up to take out the recent high at 115-23, technical analysts said on Monday.

"The picture is for a short term pull back to 114-18 then the contract should take out 115-23 ahead of 116 and a half and then 118-00," said Raynard Cheng, technical analyst at First Chicago in London.
By 0918 GMT, September T-bonds were down 2/32 at 114-31.
Cheng put initial support at 114-28 -- a level briefly touched in European time earlier and the low on July 25 -- ahead of 114-18, a level expected to hold for the time being.
Cheng said that level was the 24 percent retracement of the move from 110-23 on June 30 to 115-23 on July 23.
Below 114-18, Cheng put key support at 113-13, but added the market was unlikely to sink to that for the present.
Andy Anderson, technical analyst at Fuji Bank in London, said there was a definite uptrend on the weekly chart, with support well-established at the July 11 high of 114-15.
"There is so much data from the U.S. this week that it's just going to move on the data," he said.
The second quarter employment cost index is due on Tuesday, and the monthly payrolls data on Friday.
If 114-15 failed, the next major level of support was 113-27, the low on July 21, said Anderson.

"But it's more likely to break up," added Anderson. He said once above the latest peak of 115-23 reached on July 23, the September T-bond contract had no major resistance until 116-28, the high on December 3 on the continuation chart.
By 0928 GMT, December eurodollars were down 0.005 at 94.120. Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said as long as they held above 94.10, there was room for new highs.
